payload.title: Record the shared-store design: what hyp stores and derives when one store holds many Goals
payload.body: Design record for G1b (investigations/checkpoint-store), which builds it. Each question was settled in session e6a35a24 (2026-11-11) and is recorded as selected with that session as evidence, on the owner's decision. The decisions land in ADR 0020. No lines: no run checks a design argued in a session; G1b's lines carry the cases.

why: Owner, 2026-11-11: split G1 into a design record (G1a) and its build (G1b); create both trees.

payload.title: Two scenarios argued in the session decide which shape keeps the claims true
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: the verdict rule is two scenarios from session e6a35a24 (2026-11-11). S1: one Result cites a run at B with patch P and a run at C; a Hypothesis whose subject is bare B must not be covered. S2: 'named tests red on B, green on C' must be closable by one Result whose evidence holds both runs. A rival that breaks either is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from its scenarios.

payload.observation: S1 and S2 as argued in the session: one subject per run keeps both true; merged lists cover bare B through a patched run (S1); one base per Result leaves red on base with no single checked closer (S2). The owner chose one subject per run.

why: Session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.

payload.title: Two scenarios argued in the session decide where the start commit lives
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: S1, the base moves mid-build (main goes from B to B'); the record must stay true without a new Goal. S2, a discovery Goal has no meaningful start commit; a field only builds fill is a delivery kind, which the owner rejected. A rival that breaks either is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from its scenarios.

payload.observation: S1: a Goal field goes wrong when the base moves; the runs' subjects stay true. S2: only builds would fill it, a delivery kind. The owner agreed the Goal records no start commit, and asked that a Goal's origin be known, which is derived from its cited keys.

why: Session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.

payload.title: What is the owner's act attached to when one store holds many Goals?

why: Owner, session e6a35a24 (2026-11-11): checkpoints are one source per project, higher than a Goal.

payload.title: To no node: one owner act may move keys of several Goals; each key leads to its Goal

why: Agent's proposal in session e6a35a24 (2026-11-11).

payload.title: To one Goal: each owner act names one Goal, so one sitting across Goals is several events

why: Rival weighed in session e6a35a24 (2026-11-11).

payload.title: One owner sitting across two Goals decides what the act is attached to
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: S, one sitting accepts Goal A's referred limit and answers Goal B's open reading. The owner's rule, one checkpoint source per project, needs that sitting to be one act. A rival that needs two events, or a mechanism to name two Goals, is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from its scenario.

payload.observation: One sitting across two Goals is one act with no node; each key finds its Goal. Per-Goal acts split one sitting into several events. The owner chose no node; lines moved into the Goal's node.add, so the owner act never names a Goal.

why: Session decision, recorded as the Experiment's Result.

payload.title: Whether the envelope rule can stay per type decides the number of types
payload.body: Post hoc, on the owner's word: spec 3 and 4 define the envelope (node, why) per event type, and DecodePayload refuses unknown fields (internal/event/event.go:306). The owner and runner acts differ in the envelope. A rival whose node or why rule must depend on payload fields is contradicted.

why: Record the session's decision as an Experiment read from kongming's checked evidence.

payload.observation: The owner and runner acts differ in node and why, which the spec defines per type. Two types keep one envelope rule each and make field mixing a decode error; one type makes the envelope depend on the payload. The owner accepted two types, answer and checkpoint.
